name: Fast cool-down of a pivoted missile-seeker IR detector to 100 K within 2.3 s from a +50 C soak with a two-stage argon / CF4 (or CH4) Joule-Thomson spray cooler
plain_name: Chill a missile's infrared eye to 100 K in about two seconds with expanding high-pressure argon
description: For surface-to-air IR missiles that must be ready within seconds, a two-stage fast cool-down dual-gas spray cooler sprays argon, pre-cooled by a CF4 or CH4 first-stage Joule-Thomson cooler, through a nozzle onto the back of the gimbal-mounted detector plate; the detector reached 100 K (-173 C) in less than 2.3 s from an ambient soak of 323 K (+50 C).
keywords: Chill a missile's infrared eye to 100 K in about two seconds with expanding high-pressure argon

sources.citation: Fast-cool-down dual gas spray-cooler for pivoted IR detectors (U. Hingst, 2003), abstract

requirements.rationale: The detector is cooled to 100 K.
Mission readiness requires reaching 100 K in under 2.3 s from a +50 C soak.
The second stage expands highly pressurized, pre-cooled argon through a nozzle onto the detector plate.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
